tagline: Down the Fremont River, from green ranch country to gray shale.
intro: Highway 24 starts in the green ranch country around Loa and Bicknell and follows the Fremont River east. Toward Torrey the meadows give way to red Wingate sandstone cliffs, and in Capitol Reef the road threads the rock fins of the Waterpocket Fold. Just east of Fruita, boardwalks lead from pullouts to petroglyphs the Fremont people carved into the cliffs more than a thousand years ago.
Then the color changes again. Beyond the park the road runs out into gray and purple Mancos Shale near Caineville and Hanksville, with Factory Butte standing over the badlands.

moments.title: Loa
moments.text: The Wayne County seat was named for Mauna Loa by a Mormon missionary who had come home from Hawaii.

moments.title: Fruita
moments.text: Called the Eden of Wayne County in 1900 for its orchards, the town was bought out by the Park Service in 1955, and its 2,500 or so fruit trees are still tended.

moments.title: Giles
moments.text: A farm town first called Blue Valley for its blue-gray soil, emptied by Fremont River floods by 1919, with two rock buildings and old corrals left standing.

practical: There are no gas stations or stores for the 50 miles between Torrey and Hanksville.
